source: lead message to fastest-linux, 2026-10-04T22:5xZ, relaying Ryan: 'bugs, especially ones that make the branching slow, cannot exist'. Changing a number here is an append-only decision recorded in frontier/fastest/DECISIONS.md, never a fix for a red job.
flush_syscalls: fsync, fdatasync, syncfs, sync; msync with MS_SYNC; sync_file_range with a SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WAIT flag

full.meaning: D2: one F_FULLFSYNC-equivalent flush per flight (on Linux the engine's FullFsync class is fsync(2))
full.note: lower bounds keep a counter that reads zero from passing: at C=1 every create is its own flight; at C>1 a flight carries at most C creates, so at least one flush per C creates

async.meaning: async-durable create: no flush on the create path

instructions.metric: callgrind inclusive Ir of fastest_phase_create per op, C=1, class full, snapshot store; (Ir at 2N ops - Ir at N ops) / N

syscalls_vs_base.binds_at: C=1 only; C>1 rows are INFO (run 37400090036: same engine both sides, arm64 C=64 getpid/create 3.21 vs 3.28)

syscalls_per_create.source: frontier/fastest/DECISIONS.md 2026-10-05T02:54:27Z: the syscalls-per-create budget is ABSOLUTE on both platforms (at most 3 per create); the Linux profile job asserts the same
syscalls_per_create.counts: every syscall strace -f sees in the create window (all threads), per create, averaged over the window; the phase markers are not counted
